channel.title: Steer, Don't Guess: Blog
channel.description: Steer, Don't Guess by Martin Jirgenson: a practical method (the Jirgenson Model) for setting priorities, reading the numbers and correcting course in business and life. Kindle, paperback, hardcover and PDF.

item.title: Free sample: From the author, the Introduction and Chapter 1 of Steer, Don't Guess
item.description: Read the opening of Steer, Don't Guess by Martin Jirgenson free: From the author, the Introduction (control architecture in an age of change), the Prologue, Chapter 1 (Goal: not a dream but a list with an order, the refusal test) and the one-page cheat sheet. About 9,500 words.

item.title: Action Plan Template: Five Rows That Turn a Goal Into Monday
item.description: An action plan template with five rows: levers, resources, constraints, a leading indicator and an owner. Filled in with a freelancer's real launch plan.

item.title: Backward Planning Template: a Filled-In Example You Can Copy
item.description: A backward planning template with five columns, filled in for a freelancer's 14-month goal, plus the money check that shows if the chain really closes.

item.title: Book Launch Plan: One Page, Real Numbers, a Weekly Check
item.description: A book launch plan on one page for freelancers and first-time authors: levers, hours, budget, a sales forecast and a Monday check that catches a miss early.

item.title: Books Like The Goal: What to Read After Goldratt's Classic
item.description: Books like The Goal, matched to the five steps of the Theory of Constraints: what each one adds, which question it answers, and a ten-minute bottleneck test.

item.title: Business Crisis Plan: Write It in a Calm Week, on One Page
item.description: A business crisis plan you write before the crisis: one page, five blocks, filled in with a coffee shop's red lines and a freelancer's two-reds decision.

item.title: Business Levers: How to Find the Ones That Move Your Numbers
item.description: Business levers are what you can change by your own decision. Sort every number into lever, free parameter or outside factor, then test each lever in euros.

item.title: Cash Reserve Months of Expenses: How Long Your Money Lasts
item.description: Cash reserve months of expenses: turn the bank balance into time in ten minutes, read it against a red line, and see why a thin margin refills it so slowly.

item.title: Client Concentration Risk: How a Freelancer Went From 70% to 30%
item.description: Client concentration risk for freelancers: how to measure your largest client's share, write it as a goal with six fields, and cut it without firing anyone.

item.title: A Coffee Shop Book That Runs the Shop by the Numbers
item.description: A coffee shop book built on one owner's year: five numbers at month zero, the bin that ate the margin, a bad month, and the table that changed his Sundays.

item.title: Decision Fatigue in a Small Business: Decide Once, While Calm
item.description: Decision fatigue makes a tired owner say yes to the loudest request. Make three decisions in a calm hour, so the page decides for you when you are exhausted.

item.title: Eisenhower Matrix Alternative: Rank Your Goals, Not Your Tasks
item.description: An Eisenhower matrix alternative for owners whose every task looks urgent: rank goals once with the refusal test, then filter each request with three questions.

item.title: Goal Setting for Entrepreneurs: Put the Owner on the List
item.description: Goal setting for entrepreneurs who run the business on their own hours: write the owner row, rank it with the refusal test, and give any overload an end date.

item.title: Gut Feeling vs Numbers: How to Stop Guessing in Your Business
item.description: Your gut feeling in business is a good question and a bad answer. Turn each hunch into one measured row: a definition, one source and a number you can trust.

item.title: Household Budget in Deficit: What to Cut First, and Why
item.description: A household budget in deficit needs an order, not a fight. Read the real numbers, test each cut, pull one lever at a time, and see when the savings run out.

item.title: How Often to Review KPIs: Two Rules That Set the Rhythm
item.description: How often to review KPIs: look before a number can cross its yellow band, and judge a lever only after its loop has turned. Coffee shop numbers, no software.

item.title: How to Measure Business Performance When Your Numbers Lie
item.description: How to measure business performance honestly: audit each number for source, method and period, then check its error is small enough to steer by.

item.title: How to Prioritize Your Life Without Putting Yourself Last
item.description: How to prioritize your life when work eats every evening: put your own time on the list, write your limits first, run the refusal test and plan the exceptions.

item.title: How to Save a Failing Business: Read the Current First
item.description: How to save a failing business without a midnight rescue: check for danger, read three things in an evening, then pull one lever that moves with the market.

item.title: KPI Zones: How to Turn Any Number Into a Clear Decision
item.description: KPI zones turn a gap into a decision: work out the error, then set green, yellow and red in advance. Five steps, a freelancer's and a coffee shop's numbers.

item.title: Management Glossary in Plain English, With Coffee Shop Examples
item.description: A management glossary in plain English: goal vector, refusal order, zones, stability margin, levers, phase lag, steady mode, each with one coffee shop example.

item.title: Management Self Check: Ten Yes or No Questions for Owners
item.description: A ten-question management self check for business owners. Each No is an empty row, not a failure: it shows your weakest area and what that gap costs you.

item.title: How to Build a Management System for a Small Business in a Week
item.description: A management system for a small business is seven simple tools, not software. Build the first five in one week with one spreadsheet and a short Monday meeting.

item.title: Margin vs Markup: One Coffee Shop, Four True Numbers
item.description: Margin vs markup with one coffee shop's figures: the conversion formula, how a 15% target becomes a price rule, and why the reserve grows at the markup rate.

item.title: Measurable Goals Example: Four Lists Filled In, Field by Field
item.description: A measurable goals example from four lives: a coffee shop, a freelancer, a family in deficit and a teenager. Every field filled in, with the mistake each one exposes.

item.title: Months of Runway: How Long Your Cash Lasts, and What Is Enough
item.description: Months of runway is two numbers, not one: how many months of costs you hold, and when the money runs out at today's pace. Here is how to calculate both.

item.title: Mutually Exclusive Goals: the Arithmetic Test Before You Plan
item.description: Mutually exclusive goals cannot both be met, however hard you work. Run a ten-minute arithmetic test, then pick one of four exits: drop, cap, sequence or condition.

item.title: OKR vs Balanced Scorecard: Which One Decides on a Bad Monday?
item.description: OKR vs balanced scorecard for a small business: one words the goals, the other picks what to measure. Neither says which goal wins. One sheet does both jobs.

item.title: Phase Lag: Why Your Reports Arrive After the Damage
item.description: Phase lag is the delay between a problem and your fix. Measure your three delays, set how often to look at each number, and stop judging levers too early.

item.title: Reactive vs Proactive Management: the 15-Minute Monday Forecast
item.description: Reactive vs proactive management in one weekly habit: forecast the month on Monday, act on the gap before it lands, and let next Monday's facts correct you.

item.title: How to Teach Kids to Save Money: A Plan Your Child Runs
item.description: How to teach kids to save money: let your child write the goal, pick levers they control and count every Sunday. A 13-year-old's €300 bicycle plan, filled in.

item.title: What Is a Leading Indicator? The Weekly Number That Warns You
item.description: What is a leading indicator? A weekly number that shows a plan is working before the deadline. Write one in 15 minutes, with a filled-in example.

item.title: When to Pivot and When to Hold the Course: a Simple Test
item.description: When to pivot and when to hold the course: change the plan when the numbers miss, change the goal when conditions change, and launch big moves only on written conditions.

item.title: Backward planning: how to plan from the goal back to this week
item.description: Backward planning (reverse planning) explained with a coffee shop's second location, a free two-column template, and the five questions that tell you when it works.

item.title: Books like Measure What Matters: five to read next
item.description: Books like Measure What Matters for owners and managers, from The Goal to Traction: what each one adds, and which to read for which problem.

item.title: Business triage: what to do when everything goes wrong at once
item.description: Business triage for a bad month: seven steps from calming the noise to one decision, which problem goes first, and a coffee shop's three scenarios in numbers.

item.title: ChatGPT prompt for business decisions: a free, tested one
item.description: A free ChatGPT prompt for business decisions that was blind-tested against a good generic consultant prompt: how to use it, what to write, and what comes back.

item.title: Competing priorities: how to tell when two goals cannot both win
item.description: Competing priorities and conflicting goals explained with real numbers: how to spot two goals that cannot both win, and how to choose before a crisis does.

item.title: The control cycle: why reactive management always runs late
item.description: The control cycle in eight stages, why reactive management falls behind, and a croissant order run three ways with every error counted. PDCA side by side.

item.title: External factors in business: steer with the wind, not against it
item.description: External factors in business, from rain to rising supplier prices: how to list them, judge direction and strength, and choose a lever. Worked examples in euros.

item.title: Financial health check for a small business: one evening
item.description: A financial health check for a small business you can do in one evening: the key business metrics, where each number comes from, and how to tell a reading from a guess.

item.title: How to forecast cash flow: two lines every owner should draw
item.description: How to forecast cash flow in a small business without software: two forecasts with numbers, months until the money runs out, and a range instead of a guess.

item.title: Goal hierarchy: a prioritization method that survives a bad week
item.description: Build a goal hierarchy that decides for you on a bad day: four layers, a ranked list instead of weights, and the Eisenhower matrix put side by side with it.

item.title: How to set goals for next year as a business owner
item.description: How to set goals for next year as a business owner: a plan for tonight, this week and this month, a goals list in six areas, and a review rhythm.

item.title: How to calculate profit margin, and the cost that hides from it
item.description: How to calculate profit margin step by step, with a coffee shop worked in euros: the formula, margin vs markup, and the uncounted cost that turned 20% into 9%.

item.title: How to prevent AI hallucinations in business advice
item.description: How to prevent AI hallucinations when you ask ChatGPT or Claude for business advice: a blind test where invented facts fell from 7 answers in 10 to 1 in 120.

item.title: How to set measurable goals: six fields that turn a wish into a plan
item.description: How to set measurable goals that you can actually steer by: six fields with a worked coffee shop example, a one-minute test, and a SMART goal put through all six.

item.title: How to track write-offs in a small business before they eat margin
item.description: How to track write-offs (waste, spoiled stock, giveaways) in a small business: why they vanish from reports, a simple sheet, and what they did to one café margin.

item.title: Lagging vs leading indicators: see the result before it lands
item.description: Lagging vs leading indicators for small business owners: what each tells you, real examples for a coffee shop, a freelancer and a teenager, and how to test a leading one.

item.title: Levers of control: what you can actually change in a business
item.description: Levers of control for small business owners: how to tell a lever from a result, the three questions to ask before pulling one, and a 5% price rise tested in euros.

item.title: Management frameworks explained: OKR, BSC, PDCA, TOC and EOS
item.description: Management frameworks explained plainly: OKR, Balanced Scorecard, PDCA, TOC and EOS, one coffee shop problem run through all five.

item.title: An OKR alternative for small business: what OKRs leave out
item.description: An OKR alternative for small business: one freelancer's goals written as OKRs and as a goal vector, side by side, plus OKR vs balanced scorecard.

item.title: One page business plan: five questions for every goal
item.description: A one page business plan for each goal: five questions, a filled-in coffee shop example, a sufficiency check in numbers, and the constraint most plans forget.

item.title: Predictability in business: who is at the wheel matters most
item.description: Predictability in business lives in the pair of the work and the person running it: why one Friday is chaos for a trainee and rhythm for a pro.

item.title: How to set priorities in life when everything feels important
item.description: How to set priorities in life with one honest question: what would you give up first? A teenager, a freelancer and a family budget show the refusal test at home.

item.title: How to save for a goal: a teenager's €300 bike plan that works
item.description: How to save for a goal with a plan that survives real life: a 13-year-old's €300 bicycle fund and a family budget in deficit, worked step by step from Steer, Don't Guess.

item.title: Small business KPIs: build a dashboard you can read in a minute
item.description: Small business KPIs without software: which to track, a dashboard built in six steps, how often to measure each number, and a nine-question completeness test.

item.title: Traffic light dashboard: set red, yellow and green in advance
item.description: How to build a traffic light dashboard for a small business: where to draw the red line, what yellow asks of you, and why green means leave it alone.

item.title: Why business plans fail: three checks before you start
item.description: Why business plans fail even when you do everything right: the three offsets from Steer, Don't Guess, a coffee shop example, and when to change the plan vs the goal.

item.title: How to handle a crisis in a small business: what to do first
item.description: How to handle a crisis in a small business: the red protocol from Steer, Don't Guess, the exact order of first moves, and a coffee shop worked in euros.

item.title: Busy but not profitable: how to see it in the numbers
item.description: Busy but not profitable? How a full coffee shop with an empty till finds its real margin, and the five numbers every owner should check weekly.

item.title: The Jirgenson Model: a management method for small business owners
item.description: The Jirgenson Model by Martin Jirgenson: control theory for business and life, priorities, red lines and levers, with a glossary and an OKR comparison.

item.title: How to set priorities when everything is urgent: the refusal test
item.description: How to set priorities when everything is urgent: the refusal test from Steer, Don't Guess turns a wish list into a real order in ten seconds.
